video_title: Danny Green says Joel Embiid may be the most TALENTED big to EVER play in the NBA 🔥

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Joel Embiid's unique talent and comparison to Shaquille O'Neal
quotes.excerpt: He's a seven-footer, 300 pounds, but he could euro step and shoot step-backs.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: He's so skilled, man, and it's tough to see because you just hope you wish that he would just stay healthy. You want to see him healthy, right? Because if he was a guy that was able to stay healthy, he'd probably be one of the best bigs ever played the game because of how talented he is, his footwork. He's a seven-footer, 300 pounds, but he could euro step and shoot step-backs, do between the legs and do moves. And he's an underrated passer. But right now he's trying to get his body back and he's taking a backseat to Tyrese, but Philly's been playing pretty well this year to start. But yeah, Joel, man, he's a special talent. I haven't seen anything like it. Shaq, like he was a modern-day Shaq because he was able to do the footwork. Imagine if Shaq could shoot a jumper, a mid-range, or could make free throws.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: That's a great comparison. I could imagine that, though.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: He's able to bully you in the post still and also do moves and then also manipulate by getting fouls. Shaq was doing things to not get fouled. Joel is doing stuff to score and get fouled.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: Like a damn near guard, bro. He be funky.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: He's a seven-foot guard. It's crazy you say like, 'Oh, we'll never see this again.' But it seems like more and more these bigs keep happening. Chet, Wemby, like seven-foot-four guards.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: There's this kid in Colorado I just saw.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: Seven-footers that can handle the ball, shoot it.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: What's his name? Colorado.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: I forget his name. But I'm like, what do they keep finding these kids that are seven feet, coordinated, handle the ball, shoot threes, step-back? It's unbelievable. But Joel is in a category of his own, man. I just hope that he gets healthy and gets because I know he's hearing a lot from the Philly fans. They're not easy. But they're a blue-collar city, bro. It's one of the toughest places to play. It's not easy. So you got to come in with your hard hat on every day. And if you don't, they're going to let you know about it.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green's career-altering knee injury and contract uncertainty
quotes.excerpt: My first major injury was 13 years in the league. I did four years of college.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: Talk to us about injuries. How was how did you?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: That was a different thing for me, man. Because I was fortunate enough, I had a pretty good body. I hadn't had any major injuries my whole life. My first major injury was 13 years in the league. I did four years of college. All through high school, nothing, maybe an ankle sprain. I might have had little broken bones here, like finger, wrist, or elbow when I was young. But all through college, I played every one of the games. I think I'm in the books, I hold the records for the most wins in Carolina history throughout a four-year tenure or they probably got somebody to beat it now because they got fifth-year seniors now. But most games played and games won, you know, in that stretch, I played every, I didn't miss any games. And then even in the pros, in San Antonio, I had multiple seasons where I played 75 plus games and should have 80, 81, where Pop forced me, he rested me one or two of those games. So for me to play that long without any major injuries was great. Even the championship year, I think I had broken a wrist and sat out for four to six weeks, but nothing major where tendons or anything broke. But it was tough because I was aging and I felt like I was also playing at a high level. It was a contract year for me where I could have extended my career to play longer and still been effective. And I was hot that series. We were playing against Miami. Joel had come back, he had he had a broken face, orbital bone, something in his face.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: He came back with the mask.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: Yeah, so we played Toronto, I was playing well in Toronto. The only reason why I got, so Doc was coaching us and he was kind of messing with me a little bit during that time. It was me and Matisse. Matisse Thybulle was a really good defender. But when James came over and we traded Ben, we were like, we need somebody that's an elite defender in that starting lineup because we had James, we had Tyrese, we had Tobias, we had Joel. Then I was really the three man, I was supposed to be the three man. But then it was me and Matisse kind of switching off because he was like, we have too many guys just trying to shoot and not enough defense. So he was like, we need a defender in there. So me and Matisse kind of split time starting. The only reason why I started starting in the playoffs because Matisse never got the COVID shot. So and we had to go to Toronto. In Toronto, you couldn't play in that city unless you had your COVID shot. So then he they went to Matisse a couple times, like, 'Yo, we might end up playing, it's like a 25% chance, 30% chance we play Toronto, you sure you don't want to get these shots?' Matisse is like, 'I don't think I think I'm good. I don't think we'll end up playing them.' We ended up playing them anyway. So that gave me the opportunity to get back in the starting lineup consistently. He's like, 'All right, well, we got to move forward and make sure we keep our lineup same.' So Matisse could only play home games. But I played well that series. Joel broke his face. Next series, we in Miami. Joel missed the first two games. We get smacked in Miami the first two games in Miami. We come back home, Joel plays. I play well, I hit, you know, I'm hitting threes. I probably hit in the two games, probably total of 10 threes, maybe. Probably had like six or seven one of those games and probably like four or five.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: You like me, what that mid-level exception? You like me, what that mid-level exception?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: At least another two years, I would have been in the association another two years after that, like playing. Go to Miami, we lose again. We come back. I start off the game, I already hit a three. I'm like, all right, I'm comfortable, I'm confident at home. I'm hot. Joel goes into his bag, man, and me, because I didn't get a lot of touches, I always had to crash offensive board just to try to give myself an opportunity to get like another look or another feel for the ball.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: You know what I'm saying? You know exactly.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: You get your back cut or offensive rebound or tip out just to get a feel for the basketball. So I had a habit of crashing the offensive glass just to give get a second opportunity. I go into crash from the PJ Tucker. Joel goes into his move and he falls and I'm looking up and it happened so fast, I couldn't get my leg out of there. He rolled right into my leg. And I just felt my whole thing just. I was like, oh, sh*t, it's over. I thought it was out. Honestly, I thought it was out the socket. I didn't look. I was telling them to pop it back in. I was telling them to pop it back in. And I looked down, my leg was still straight. I was like, oh, sh*t, thank God. Like, I thought it was like out the socket, out the bone, something.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Damn.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: I was like, it's over, bro. There's no way.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: What did it end up being?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: ACL, LCL, little bit of hamstring, little bit of IT band.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: No surgery.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: I'm familiar with that. I'm familiar with that.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Six-hour surgery.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: Yeah, six-hour surgery.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: At this time, I'm assuming the doctors are like, how are y'all today?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: Yeah, so they like, well, my biggest concern was my contract at the time was not guaranteed for the next year. So I signed a one-and-one. And I was like, damn, so I might be cut out the league and not have no contract. I'm not getting paid for my second year. So I'm like, I got to find a place to rehab or somebody's going to cover the rehab and then try to get back in or stay with a team, stay with a group. And they already predicted I'm going to be out the whole year next year anyway. I'm discouraged, like, sh*t. This is like May. But after doing some research, people are like, no, people come back. But this is a double ligament tear. Most people come back from ACL tear, you can come back six, seven months if you do it right. So if you go to May, you could probably come back following year, midway through the year. Most double ligaments take forever, but I was lucky enough to come back still by that following January, like eight months later, seven, eight months later. But I got traded to Memphis and Memphis picked up my contract and then it got fully guaranteed after a certain point. That's when I was there rehabbing and got a chance to be around the young guys and being a tax-free state and collect more a little check.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Yeah.
